name: Malimpung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Hanafie, Sitti Hawang, Kulla Lagousi, Moha Junaedie, Siti Hafsah J. Nur & Muhammad Sikki. 1983. Morfologi dan sintaksis bahasa Massenrempulu. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Earlier Pusat Bahasa description of Massenrempulu; introductory chapters of this series often summarise phonology including stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Malimpung [mli]. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Free tier shows classification/vitality only; no typology or stress information visible.

sources.citation: Saupia, Renhard. 2024. Kesalingmengertian rumpun bahasa Massenrempulu: Duri, Enrekang, Maiwa, dan Malimpung di Sulawesi. Linguistik Indonesia 42(1), 141-155. doi:10.26499/li.v42i1.553
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (intelligibility testing; no occurrence of tekanan/stress).

sources.citation: Saupia, Renhard, Tiar Simanjuntak, Geraldy Ruwayari & Maggie Canvin. 2023. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Massenrempulu Language Cluster of South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-006. Dallas: SIL International. 36 pp. (SIL archive entry 97924; archived copy (Internet Archive, 8 May 2025) of the sil.org reapdata PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement on stress anywhere in the report. Appendix A (pp. 15-22, Table 9) gives a 264-item Malimpung wordlist (Malimpung village, 19 Sep 2019) in handwritten-then-typed IPA with a stress mark ' preceding the stressed syllable; script tally of first form per item (vowel groups as nuclei): 164 penult, 50 antepenult (many of these are prefixed verbs with the mark written word-initially, e.g. 'manasu 'cook', 'matinro 'sleep'), 12 final (mostly forms ending in a vowel sequence, e.g. ma'buang), 4 pre-antepenult, 34 unmarked. Raw data only, no rule stated.

sources.citation: Simanjuntak, Tiar. 2022 [KIMLI 2021]. Is Malimpung [mli] a dialect of Bugis [bug]? Kongres Internasional Masyarakat Linguistik Indonesia, 385-389. doi:10.51817/kimli.vi.84
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics (68% with Bugis), RTT, language attitudes only.

sources.citation: Syamsul Rijal. 2010. Sistem bunyi bahasa Massenrempulu dialek Maiwa. Sawerigading 16(1), 52-60. Makassar: Balai Bahasa Ujung Pandang.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes MAIWA [wmm], the Massenrempulu lect lexically closest to Malimpung, not Malimpung itself: 5 vowels, 19 consonants, phoneme distribution table, syllable types V/VK/KV/KVK; no section or remark on tekanan/stress.

sources.citation: Friberg, Timothy & Thomas V. Laskowske. 1989. South Sulawesi languages. In J.N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi Linguistics Part 1 (NUSA 31), 1-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; p. 5 reports Malimpung (5000 speakers) was found by the Bugis dialect survey and shown by Valkama to be 'clearly a Masenrempulic speech form'.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Malimpung is not mentioned anywhere (their Masenrempulu word lists are Enrekang and Maiwa). Areal note only, printed p. 94 (PDF p. 102), Symbols: 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern.. it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable.'

sources.citation: Valkama, Kari. 1987. Kabupatens Pinrang, Enrekang, Tana Toraja, Luwu and eastern part of Polewali Mamasa. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL South Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys 1983-1987 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 5), 119-136. Jayapura: Percetakan Universitas Cenderawasih.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The UNHAS-SIL survey that first identified Malimpung as a Masenrempulu lect; SIL survey chapters of this series sometimes carry brief phonological notes and stress-marked wordlists. Only Glottolog-listed reference for the language.

sources.citation: Balai Bahasa Ujung Pandang. 2000-2001. Kamus Dialek Massenrempulu Maiwa-Indonesia, Bagian I (A-K) and Bagian II. Risalah Penelitian Balai Bahasa Ujung Pandang. Makassar. (cited in Syamsul Rijal 2010)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Maiwa dictionary; front matter of Balai Bahasa dictionaries usually has an ejaan/fonologi note that may mention tekanan. Maiwa is the Massenrempulu lect lexically closest to Malimpung (66-68% in JLSR 2023-006 Table 7).

sources.citation: Sikki, Muhammad et al. 1997. Tata bahasa Massenrempulu. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan.

sources.note: Pusat Bahasa grammar of Massenrempulu (Enrekang/Maiwa/Duri); such grammars normally include a fonologi chapter with a 'tekanan' paragraph. Would give the closest first-hand stress statement for the cluster Malimpung belongs to (not Malimpung itself).

sources.citation: Mills, Roger F. 1975. Proto South Sulawesi and Proto Austronesian Phonology. 2 vols. PhD dissertation, University of Michigan.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Synchronic phonology sketches (including stress) of each South Sulawesi language used in the reconstruction; treats Massenrempulu as one transitional lect. Areal/cluster-level evidence only.
